name: Glen Industries Ltd
title: Glen Industries Ltd - 544444 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Glen Industries H2 FY26 PAT of INR8.20 crore on INR108.60 crore income; management targets INR500 crore turnover and INR90 crore EBITDA in FY28.
summary.overview: FY26 total income was INR205.16 crore, EBITDA INR38.50 crore and PAT INR16.50 crore, with H2 FY26 income of INR108.60 crore, EBITDA INR18.69 crore and PAT INR8.20 crore. Management attributed margin compression from about 23-24% in FY25 to about 18-19% in FY26 to passing on PLA price benefits to customers. A capacity expansion (plastic food containers roughly 3x, plus about 750 MT paper-based food packaging including paper cups) has a revised project cost of INR130-135 crore, now expected to start commercial production from September 2026. Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict, with polypropylene peaking near INR150/kg and now about INR135/kg.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin FY26 (as cited on call)
financial_highlights.change: down from about 23-24% in FY25 per management and analyst

financial_highlights.value: Thin-wall food containers 82.72%; PLA and paper straws 17.16%; mould designing 0.12%

segments.name: Thin-wall food containers
segments.commentary: About 82.72% of FY26 revenue with capacity utilisation of about 77.74%. Raw-material price pass-through is monthly, impacting turnover by about INR2.5 crore per month during the recent price rise.

segments.name: PLA and paper straws
segments.commentary: About 17.16% of FY26 revenue; utilisation about 28.33% (PLA) and 34.13% (paper). Management says these are seasonal, peak-season-only (4-4.5 months), and sees utilisation capped near 35%; no further straw capex planned.

guidance_outlook: FY28 target: turnover above INR500 crore with EBITDA of about INR90 crore (about 18-19% margin), based on pre-war raw material prices.
Expansion revenue: existing capacity about INR200-215 crore; new project adds about INR300 crore; combined about INR500 crore per annum.
FY27 incremental revenue from new capacity estimated at INR100-125 crore, depending on stabilisation speed; some revenue expected in FY27.
Commercial production targeted from September 2026, with full project operational by October-December 2026.
Management says EBITDA margin sustainable at 18-19% over the long run; paper cup margin around 18%.
Eight additional injection moulding machines (20 to 29) expected to add about INR15 crore annual revenue.
capex_capacity: Expansion project cost revised to INR130-135 crore from about INR100 crore, citing rupee depreciation (85-86 to about 96 per USD-equivalent as stated), wider scope in building and machinery, and printing machines.
Funding: INR50 crore term loan and INR50 crore IPO proceeds for original INR100 crore; incremental INR30-32 crore from internal accruals; no additional debt or equity planned.
Commissioning delayed about three months due to SIR and West Bengal elections holding up building plan approvals; commercial production now expected from September 2026.
Injection moulding machines raised from 20 to 29.
Existing land parcel remains mortgaged to bank; to be released after new facility is capitalised.
Management says no further straw capex; straw capacity sufficient for demand.
demand_pricing: PLA price about INR205/kg now vs INR195-197/kg pre-war; polypropylene about INR135/kg now vs INR90-92/kg pre-war, peaking near INR150/kg; paper stable (locally sourced).
Pass-through: PLA price changes passed on to customers from March; food container prices adjusted monthly; management says absolute margin preserved though percentage margin falls.

Raw material sourcing: about 85% imported (mainly Middle East earlier), 15% from Indian Oil; imported material from China at 5-6% price advantage; Middle East supply expected to normalise in 1-2 months.
Raw material inventory above 3 months currently; finished goods 2-2.5 months.

Customer concentration: no customer above 5-6% of total sales; top 4-5 export customers (US, UK, Greece) account for about 50-60% of export sales; over 300 domestic distributors; Parle about 25% of corporate sales as stated.
Exports: about 40 recurring international clients across Europe, US, Australia, South Korea; export revenue declined in FY26 due to lower polymer prices vs FY25, not volume or war.
Geography: eastern India about 35% of revenue; north and west next.
Competition: few national/export players in India with HACCP and FSSC certifications; management cites brand and standards as barriers.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline and what is the sustainable range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PLA price benefits were passed to customers in FY26, lowering margin from about 23% (FY25) to about 18-19%; sustainable range stated as 18-19%.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion capex, timeline and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Project cost revised to INR130-135 crore; commercial production from September 2026, full operations by December 2026; combined revenue potential about INR500 crore per annum.

qa_highlights.question: Utilisation of straws and paper products given seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straw utilisation can not exceed about 35% due to 4-4.5 month peak season; paper cups are not currently manufactured, and the expansion includes paper cups with about 18% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of raw material price rise on FY27 turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about INR2-2.5 crore per month turnover uplift from price pass-through, with no change to absolute margin; guidance remains based on pre-war prices.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any production disruption from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no disruption; about two months of inventory was held and two months' requirement was imported from China.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: PP and PLA prices remain elevated; management says guidance excludes current prices and could reverse within about two months of conflict ending.
Margin percentage compression in price-rising periods; EBITDA margin moved from about 17-18% to higher levels in prior halves.
Execution risk on the new project: approvals delayed about three months, commissioning expected September 2026, with capacity ramp-up pace determining FY27 revenue.
Seasonal demand in straws (beverage sector) keeping utilisation low around 28-34%.
Working capital build: raw material inventory above 3 months and inventory cycle of 5-5.5 months against about 4 months normal, affecting ROCE.
Customer and export concentration: top export accounts about 50-60% of export sales.
Undisclosed land parcel and future diversification plans; management declined to specify new products.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing pass-through and FY28 targets, but defensive when questioned on margin decline and straw utilisation. Several answers were repetitive or unclear, and management declined to disclose future product plans.
key_quotes: So, if we add both of them, existing capacity and the additional capacity, we will be able to achieve a turnover of INR500 crores per annum going forward.
We always have been maintaining that our EBITDA margin will be within 18% to 19%.
We are not projecting on the basis of increased promising prices. We are projecting on the stable prices before the war.
No customer is more than, you can say, 5% to 6% of our total sales.

adds.what: Plastic food container capacity expansion (~3x) plus ~750 MT paper-based food packaging incl. paper cups, with 8 extra injection moulding machines (20 to 29)

growth.why: Management targets turnover above INR500 crore and EBITDA of about INR90 crore in FY28 (from INR205 crore FY26 income), backed by a INR130-135 crore expansion starting commercial production from September 2026 and FY27 incremental revenue of INR100-125 crore; the backing is partly specific but no order book or contracts are cited.
